text:
anna: CI alert  nightly-edge-tests failing for the onboarding-suite. Both vitest & jest show different failures but same root cause: ESM/CJS module identity mismatch for runtime mocks (fetch/kvMock).

dev-bot: nightly-onboarding  build/onboarding #814 failed
```Error: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at wrapSafe (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1054:15)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader:1092:27)
```

chris: quick local repro: `pnpm -w test --filter=@redwood/sdk -- run unit` with node 20. Vitest resolves exports.import -> dist/runtime.mjs; jest + ts-jest sometimes resolves require -> dist/runtime.cjs because of transformIgnorePatterns. Our test mocks patch the cjs runtime, so when vitest loads mjs the mock isn't present.

rachel: saw this too. Additional wrinkle: ts-jest + isolatedModules can cause different transpilation paths so the compiled mock ends up with different symbol names. Also some folks import `@redwood/sdk/runtime` while others import `@redwood/sdk` and rely on re-exports -> multiple module identities.

tom: minimal fixes I applied that made CI green on linux/mac:
1) Add a CJS test shim: `tests/shims/runtime-require.cjs`:
```js
// tests/shims/runtime-require.cjs
const { createRequire } = require('module');
const req = createRequire(import.meta.url || __filename);
module.exports = req('../../dist/runtime.cjs');
```
2) jest.config.js snippet:
```js
module.exports = {
  transformIgnorePatterns: ['node_modules/(?!@redwood/sdk)'],
  moduleNameMapper: { '^@redwood/sdk/(.*)$': '<rootDir>/tests/shims/runtime-require.cjs' }
}
```
3) vitest.config.ts: inline the package so vite doesn't fold to import entry:
```ts
export default defineConfig({ test: { deps: { inline: ['@redwood/sdk'] } } })
```

anna: I also added a tiny setup file for vitest that explicitly imports `../../dist/runtime.mjs` and attaches the same mocks we use in jest. That ensures both runners set global.fetch the same way.

chris: alternative approach we discussed: publish an explicit "test" export in package.json to force the CJS variant in CI, e.g. "{ \"exports\": { \"./runtime\": { \"test\": \"./dist/runtime.cjs\", \"import\": \"./dist/runtime.mjs\" } } }" and set NODE_OPTIONS to enable experimental loader that picks the test field. Not ideal. The shim + inline feels less invasive.

rachel: Another gotcha: Windows runners failed until we changed shim path to use forward slashes and avoided long path names. Make sure the shim path is relative to repo root and not to workspace package root.

anna: Also fixed TypeScript typings: add `types` root entry pointing to `dist/runtime.d.ts` and add `exports.types` entry so editors/tsc pick up types regardless of which export path is chosen. That removed a lot of noise from ts-jest.

tom: I pushed a small PR to mono that: adds the CJS shim, updates jest/vitest configs in the onboarding package, and publishes the types mapping. CI green on linux/mac. Windows flake rate dropped significantly. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/pull/901

chris: long-term idea: maintain a small `runtime-testing` package that's CJS-only with the mock hooks. Consumers can depend on it in devDependencies and both runners will import the same module identity. Could be cleaner than shimming package exports.

rachel: agreed that would be cleaner for onboarding repos. But we should standardize the devex doc first: include shim pattern, vitest deps.inline, jest moduleNameMapper, types mapping, and the runtime-testing package option. I'll draft the page.

anna: thanks all. I've updated the edge test pipeline to include the shim by default. Re-running nightly now. Reopen if any new stack traces show up. :white_check_mark:
